newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa searches for survivors after ship sinks.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa searches for survivors after ship sinks.

text.p: Rescuers have recovered three bodies after a Panamanian cargo ship sank off South Africa's Indian Ocean coast with 29 crewmen on board, port officials said on Thursday.
"We have three bodies that have been picked from the sea so far," port of Durban captain Ron Holloway told Reuters.

He said all 29 crewmen from the 12,000 tonne mixed-cargo vessel named Cordigliera were feared killed after it hit rough seas about five nautical miles east of Port St Johns on South Africa's Wild Coast early on Thursday.
"There are 29 crewmen whom we assume have been killed in the incident," Holloway said. "The last report from the ship was: 'I am taking in water, I need assistance'."
Patches of debris including three-badly damaged life rafts, one capsised lifeboat as well as paper reels and a patch of oil have been found near where the ship ran aground.
Holloway said the ship set off from Durban on Wednesday morning and had been en route for Cape Town and the West African cities of Abidjan and Lagos before it began taking in water in heavy swells.

"The sea around the area is not pleasant but our search and rescue teams are going to continue searching for more bodies," he said. Two South African Air Force helicopters are assisting in the search.
